intro: This awareness course covered supporting people with additional communication needs — recognising barriers, using the right tools, and working in a person-centred way.
points: This is awareness only — you support communication and follow the plan, while a speech and language therapist assesses and advises.
Communication is a human right linked to dignity, choice and safety; never assume difficulty speaking means difficulty thinking.
Presume competence, look for barriers you can remove, and use total communication — words, gesture, pictures, objects and signing together.
Give people time to process and respond, ask one thing at a time, and never rush or answer for them.
Treat an AAC device as the person's voice — keep it charged, clean and within reach, and never speak for them.
Check understanding gently rather than accepting a nod, follow the communication care plan, and record clearly what works so everyone benefits.
